Estimate a log-log price association

Source: R/elasticity.R
estimate_price_elasticity.Rd

Fits log(rounds) on log(price) with optional linear controls and optional group fixed effects. The price coefficient is the percent change in rounds associated with a 1 percent higher price in the rows that remain, under this specification.

Usage

estimate_price_elasticity(
  data,
  rounds,
  price,
  controls = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  min_n = 30,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  exclusion_warn = 0.1
)

Arguments

data

A table.

rounds, price

Column names. Both must be positive in a row that enters the fit.

controls

Optional column names entered as linear terms. Numeric or logical columns only. Pass categories through group.

group

Optional column names entered as fixed effects.

min_n

Minimum number of rows after exclusions.

conf_level

Confidence level for the ordinary least-squares interval.

exclusion_warn

Warn when the unique excluded share of the supplied rows is at least this fraction. The default is 10 percent.

Value

A golfops_elasticity list. model is the stats::lm() fit. limitations states the deviations from the Enz and Canina specification and the inferential limits of this fit.

Details

The standard error and confidence interval come from stats::lm(). They are ordinary least-squares statistics. Enz and Canina clustered standard errors by course. These are not clustered estimates. Passing a course identifier to group adds a fixed effect. It does not cluster the standard errors.

Their working-paper equation, page 8, regresses log rounds on log average daily price, course age, rating, slope, number of holes, regular-tee par, water features, lodging, minimum temperature, precipitation, location indicators, and a year fixed effect. Temperature in that equation is degrees Fahrenheit and precipitation is inches. This function adds a control or a group only when you name the column. It does not convert units. A numeric control enters as a straight line. A column named in group enters as a set of fixed effects.

The logarithm is defined for positive numbers. Rows with a missing, zero, or negative rounds or price value are excluded, as are rows with a missing control or group value. n_excluded counts each excluded row once. exclusions counts each reason, so one row can appear in more than one reason. A warning is issued when the unique excluded share reaches exclusion_warn. The published transaction file is not public, and this function does not re-estimate the published coefficients. A coefficient is not a causal demand elasticity and not a recommendation to change a posted price.

References

Enz, Cathy A., and Linda Canina. 2016. "Competitive Pricing in the Golf Industry." Cornell University, School of Hotel Administration. https://hdl.handle.net/1813/72428. The log-log specification and course-clustered standard errors are on page 8 of that working paper. Journal version: Journal of Revenue and Pricing Management 16 (2): 139–153. doi:10.1057/s41272-016-0075-8 .

Examples

sample <- simulate_elasticity_sample(
  "correct_specification",
  n_days = 80,
  seed = 457
)
estimate_price_elasticity(
  sample,
  rounds = "rounds",
  price = "price",
  controls = c("weekend", "temp_min_c", "precip_mm")
)
#> Log-log price association
#> log(rounds) ~ log(price) + weekend + temp_min_c + precip_mm
#> Elasticity -0.801; OLS standard error 0.046; 95% interval [-0.891, -0.710]
#> Rows used 80 of 80 (0.0% excluded).
#> 
#> A coefficient of -0.801 is the ordinary least-squares association between log rounds and log price in the rows that remain. It is the percent change in rounds associated with a 1 percent higher price under this specification. The standard error is not clustered by course. The coefficient is not a causal demand elasticity and not a recommendation to change a posted price.
#> 
#> - This is a methodological analogue of Enz and Canina (2016), working paper page 8. It does not re-estimate their published coefficients. Their transaction data are not public.
#> - The published equation uses log rounds, log average daily price, course characteristics, minimum temperature in degrees Fahrenheit, precipitation in inches, location indicators, and a year fixed effect.
#> - The standard error and confidence interval are ordinary least-squares statistics from lm(). They are not standard errors clustered by course.
#> - A column in group is a fixed effect. It does not cluster the standard errors. Course characteristics, weather, location, and year are included only when those columns are named.
#> - Rows with missing, zero, or negative rounds or prices are excluded because a logarithm is defined for positive numbers. The excluded share can change the sample when the omitted rows are closures or missing prices.
#> - The coefficient is the association in the rows that remain under this specification. It is not a causal price elasticity. It is not a recommendation to change a posted price. A positive coefficient is not evidence that demand rises with price.
#> - Rounds played can be censored at capacity. This fit does not correct for that.
#> - An average of prices paid is not a posted rack rate. A shift in customer mix can move that average and total rounds together.
#> - A synthetic sample can recover a known coefficient when the data are generated from the fitted equation. That check is not a description of Dobson Ranch. Dobson realized green-fee yield is not a posted price.
